ai.baseUrlHint: The address of the server's OpenAI-compatible API, for example http://localhost:1234/v1 for LM Studio.
ai.contextSizeHintOllamaLimit: How much text the app asks Ollama to read in one request. 32k fits everything the app sends: a CV, a posting or a careers page with the answer. More only takes more memory; less can leave long careers pages unread. This model takes up to {{limit}} tokens. Ollama's own context setting does not limit it.
ai.contextSizeHint: How many tokens the server reads in one request; its own settings say so. The app uses it to spot texts that are too long: a longer posting is not scored and a longer CV is flagged, instead of being cut without notice.

test.hint: Saves your changes, then tests the provider, model and key.

reasons.unreachable: the provider could not be reached

ai.contextSizeHintOllama: How much text the app asks Ollama to read in one request. 32k fits everything the app sends: a CV, a posting or a careers page with the answer. More only takes more memory; less can leave long careers pages unread. Ollama's own context setting does not limit it.

help.anthropic: Claude models, in the cloud. Create an API key in the Anthropic Console and paste it below. Your CV and job texts are sent to Anthropic.
help.openai: GPT models, in the cloud. Create an API key on the OpenAI platform and paste it below. Your CV and job texts are sent to OpenAI.
help.gemini: Gemini models, in the cloud. Create an API key in Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com) and paste it below. Your CV and job texts are sent to Google; on the free tier Google may use them to improve its models.
help.ollama: Runs on this computer: no key, and nothing leaves your machine. Install Ollama from ollama.com, open it, then download a model in the terminal, for example: ollama pull {{example}}
help.openaiCompatible: Any server with an OpenAI-compatible API, such as LM Studio or vLLM. Enter its address and, if it asks for one, a key.
help.none: Nothing is sent to any AI. The profile is filled in by hand and the jobs are not scored by affinity; the rest of the app works as usual. You can turn the AI on later.

ollama.empty: Ollama is running but has no models. Download one in the terminal, for example: ollama pull {{example}}, then refresh the list.

ai.geminiModelHint: The model name as Google AI Studio shows it, starting with gemini-. A Flash model is fast and cheap for scoring many jobs.

search.intro: The app looks on the web for the companies hiring for the roles in your profile and for their job pages, and when you search on the Sources page. It starts with DuckDuckGo, which is free.
search.keysIntro: DuckDuckGo sometimes blocks automated searches. When it does, the services below take over, in this order, and only the ones with a key. Each has a free plan with a monthly limit: when one runs out, the next one takes over.

updates.hint: Looks at GitHub Releases for a newer version. Nothing else is sent.

review.title: Review of your profile
review.intro: What could be better in your profile, checked against the postings for your roles. The advice is for you to apply by hand: nothing here changes your profile.
review.loadFailed: The review could not be loaded.
review.noFindings: The checks found nothing to fix.
review.market: Skills compared with {{count}} postings for your roles.

rules.no-headline: No headline. One line saying who you are professionally helps, for example "Backend engineer, TypeScript and PostgreSQL".
rules.no-summary: No summary. Two or three sentences on what you do and what you look for help the reader and the matching.
rules.short-summary: The summary is only {{length}} characters. A few sentences give the matching more to work with.
rules.no-experience: No experience listed. Add your roles, even short ones, that show the skills you want to use.
rules.experience-no-bullets_one: {{count}} role has no detail. Say what you did there, with a result where you can.
rules.experience-no-bullets_other: {{count}} roles have no detail. Say what you did in each, with a result where you can.
rules.no-numbers: None of your {{count}} bullets contains a figure. A number (time saved, users, size) makes a result believable.
rules.no-skills: No skills listed. The matching and your documents start from this list.
rules.few-skills_one: Only {{count}} skill listed. Add the tools you really use, with the names job posts use.
rules.few-skills_other: Only {{count}} skills listed. Add the tools you really use, with the names job posts use.
rules.unbacked-skills: {{count}} listed skills are never mentioned in your work: {{skills}}. A skill with an example behind it is more convincing.
rules.no-education: No education listed. Add it, or a course, if it supports the roles you look for.
rules.no-links: No links. A portfolio, GitHub or LinkedIn page lets a reader check your work.
rules.no-roles: No target roles. Without them the app cannot look for companies or tell which jobs fit you.
rules.no-places: No places. Add where you want to work, or the app shows jobs from anywhere.
rules.market-skill-missing: {{skill}} is named in {{percent}}% of the postings for your roles ({{jobs}} postings) and nowhere in your profile. If you know it, add it; if not, it may be worth learning.

This application is not sent yet. To finish it:

2. Open the company's form: the app fills in what it can, and you check it and send it yourself.
